title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
main_claim: For every minimal homeomorphism h of an infinite compact metrizable space X, rc(C(X)⋊_h Z) = mdim(X,h)/2 in [0,∞]. This is the integer-action case of the Phillips–Toms conjecture. As a corollary, zero mean dimension, the small boundary property, Z-stability, finite nuclear dimension and nuclear dimension ≤ 1 are all equivalent. The lower bound is new. The upper bound is Niu's Theorem 5.6.
coverage:
Read all six sections. Checked:
(1) The uniform block allocation lemma: the tower from Niu's Theorem 4.2, the sets B and O_i with h^{i+Dk}O_i ⊂ B, the compactness argument over invariant measures giving uniformly small μ(C), and the orbit-count bound via weak limits of empirical measures.
(2) The trace gap: d_τ is the integral of the rank, and (R−pg)μ(B) > r gives P_0 ≾ P_1.
(3) The finite-propagation Cuntz witness: the corner extraction is valid, Fourier truncation is valid, and ‖W_Jξ‖² ≥ ½‖ξ‖² holds on the 1-eigenspace of π_x(P_0).
(4) The k-separation of active rows and the generic coordinate-compression maps C_J and D_J; the kernel argument for Φ1⊕Φ2; continuity across changes in the sparse support. The rank estimate K_J/(pn) → RH_0/(pg(H_0−1)) + 2(a+b_0) < 2 checks out.
(5) Packet reconstruction: Z ≥ 1−2gτ > 1/2, no new colors appear, and the carrier dimension is at most m−s.
(6) Theorem 5.1:
- The parameter arithmetic: (2−10a)H_0/(H_0−1) < 2−8a, and lim(E_k−d) < −ac_0/64.
- The edge blocks cover [0,e).
- The join map is continuous.
- The good/bad interval carrier-dimension count gives uNE_k.
- The polyhedral refinement step holds, and E_k < d contradicts d = inf m_k/k.
(7) The regularity corollary (Rørdam, CETWW, Lindenstrauss–Weiss/Lindenstrauss).
I also compared the interface with the companion paper's Theorem 1.3 (cobordism paper): t, L ⊂ (−1/32,1/32)^t, H, Z_an, a < 1/16, the a/8 fraction and the boundary-preservation clause all match verbatim. I did not re-audit the companion's proof; the sibling branch reported no gap there. I did not independently verify Niu's Theorems 4.2 and 5.6 beyond checking that their hypotheses hold (freeness and the marker property).
